s1.syndrome_frame: Fetal neurological abnormalities with ventriculomegaly and irregular ventricular walls
salient_findings: Multiple hyperechoic regions within the ventricular lumens
key_facts: Normal middle cerebral artery perfusion on fetal Doppler ultrasound
Bilateral ventricular enlargement on fetal MRI
Areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images within the ventricles
Comprehensive workup returned within normal limits

raw.syndrome_frame: Fetal neurological abnormalities with ventriculomegaly and irregular ventricular walls
salient_findings: Multiple hyperechoic regions within the ventricular lumens
key_facts: Normal middle cerebral artery perfusion on fetal Doppler ultrasound
Bilateral ventricular enlargement on fetal MRI
Areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images within the ventricles
Comprehensive workup returned within normal limits

shortlist.label: Congenital Cytomegalovirus Infection
shortlist.why_kept: Fetal neurological abnormalities with ventriculomegaly and irregular ventricular walls are consistent with congenital CMV infection

shortlist.label: Congenital Toxoplasmosis
shortlist.why_kept: Fetal ventriculomegaly and irregular ventricular walls can be seen in congenital toxoplasmosis

shortlist.label: Dandy-Walker Malformation
shortlist.why_kept: Bilateral ventricular enlargement and areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images are consistent with Dandy-Walker malformation

shortlist.label: Congenital Lymphocytic Choriomeningitis
shortlist.why_kept: Fetal neurological abnormalities and ventriculomegaly can be seen in congenital lymphocytic choriomeningitis

shortlist.label: Aicardi-Goutieres Syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Fetal ventriculomegaly and irregular ventricular walls, along with normal comprehensive workup, are consistent with Aicardi-Goutieres syndrome

raw.rationale: The presence of bilateral ventriculomegaly, irregular ventricular walls, and multiple hyperechoic regions within the ventricular lumens on ultrasound, along with areas of high signal intensity on T1-weighted images and low signal intensity on T2-weighted images within the ventricles on MRI, are consistent with congenital CMV infection, which can cause these characteristic neuroimaging findings.

rejected.label: Congenital Toxoplasmosis
rejected.why: While toxoplasmosis can cause similar neuroimaging findings, the comprehensive workup including a TORCH panel returned within normal limits, making this less likely.

rejected.label: Dandy-Walker Malformation
rejected.why: Dandy-Walker malformation typically presents with hypoplasia of the cerebellar vermis and cystic dilation of the fourth ventricle, which were not described in this case.

rejected.label: Congenital Lymphocytic Choriomeningitis
rejected.why: The normal comprehensive workup makes this diagnosis less likely, as LCMV infection would likely be detected in the TORCH panel or through other laboratory tests.

rejected.label: Aicardi-Goutieres Syndrome
rejected.why: This syndrome typically presents with more severe and early onset neurological symptoms, and the described neuroimaging findings do not specifically suggest Aicardi-Goutieres Syndrome.
